title: Compressed-graph invariance for similarly factored ideals in UFD quotients
statement:
Let $D_1$ and $D_2$ be unique factorization domains, and let $I_1\subset D_1$ and $I_2\subset D_2$ be nonmaximal, nontrivial ideals. Suppose

$$
I_1=\bigcup_{\alpha\in\Lambda}\left\langle\prod_{k=1}^{Q_\alpha}p_{\alpha_k}^{s_{\alpha_k}}\right\rangle.
$$

Assume that $I_2$ has an expression with the same index set, numbers of factors, and exponents,

$$
I_2=\bigcup_{\alpha\in\Lambda}\left\langle\prod_{k=1}^{Q_\alpha}q_{\alpha_k}^{s_{\alpha_k}}\right\rangle.
$$

Here the $p_{\alpha_k}$ and $q_{\alpha_k}$ are the corresponding irreducible factors.

**Compressed-graph invariance conjecture.** Under these hypotheses,

$$
\Gamma_C(D_1/I_1)\cong\Gamma_C(D_2/I_2).
$$

Thus the compressed zero-divisor graph is conjectured to depend only on the displayed factorization pattern of the ideal, not on the particular UFDs or irreducibles.
source_name: Rachael Alvir, “Zero-Divisor Graphs of Quotient Rings”, arXiv:1508.02432 (2015).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1508.02432

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2015).
